doc.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995

title: Vocal coaching Marilyn Monroe and film musicals
summary: Through Jackie Mills and Jack Cole he coached Monroe for her musicals and recalls a few film titles.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Yeah. When did you start doing, you did some vocal coaching in the studios out here?
I did a little of it yeah.
How did you get into that?
Well people would call me since I’d worked with Lena and all the different people they figured I knew something about singers. I started believing them too.
And you would do that for the studios?

Oh, no, the only person I really coached in the studio was Marilyn Monroe. I got that job through Jackie Mills who used to be a drummer with Tommy Dorsey, and he had an in with Jack Cole, the choreographer. So he took me out of the studio one day and Jack Cole liked what I did so every time Marilyn did a musical, I was there.
I read that it took her a lot of takes to get, in films sometimes. Is that true?

Well she wasn’t a singer per se you know, but she worked hard at it. And Jack Cole changed her style so much. He gave her things to do that she could half talk and half sing. So it came off pretty good for her.
Did you, were you involved with “Some Like It Hot?”
Well yeah, but that was mostly, what was it Jack Lemmon? Who was in that?
And Tony Curtis, yeah. And I didn’t have too much to do with that but I was in “Les Girls,” what is it “Let’s Make Love,” about five or six of them.
